chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man and his wife upon whom a house fell, and he said: 'The wife inherits from the man, then the man inherits from the wife.'
And from him from Fadalah from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon both of them): similar to that.

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: one of them (referring to an Imam)

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided between a husband and wife who die at the same time?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential principle of simultaneous death (*mawt jamīʿ*), where neither spouse is presumed to have predeceased the other, allowing for mutual inheritance. This ruling prevents the estate from being absorbed by one party's heirs exclusively, ensuring a balanced distribution that reflects the concurrent nature of their demise. It serves as a foundational text for resolving complex inheritance scenarios in Shia fiqh when the order of death cannot be determined.
